chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Sayf, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Thānī عليه السلام; and Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn Aslam, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān and Yūnus ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: We asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man from whom some people sought help so that he might rescue them from a people raiding them in order to seize their property and enslave their children. So the man went out running with his weapon in

the middle of the night to aid the people who had sought his help. He passed by a man standing at the edge of a well drawing water from it, and he pushed him while not intending that and not realizing it, so the man fell into the well and died. The man continued on and rescued the property of those people who had sought his help. When he returned to his family, they said to him: What did you do? He said: The people turned away from them, and they became safe and unharmed. They said to him: Did you know that so-and-so son of so-and-so fell into the well and died? He said: By Allah, I was the one who threw him in. It was said: How was that? He said: I went out running with my weapon in the darkness of the night while fearing that I might miss reaching the people who had sought my help. I passed by so-and-so while he was standing drawing water from the well, and I jostled him, not intending that, so he fell and died. Then upon whom is the blood-money for this? He said: “His blood-money is upon the people who sought the man’s aid, and he came to their aid and saved their property, their women, and their children. However, if he had hired himself out for a wage, then the blood-money would have been upon him and upon his ʿāqilah, not upon them.

And that is because Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd عليه السلام was approached by an elderly woman seeking redress against the wind. She said: O Prophet of Allah, I was standing on a roof, and the wind cast me down from the roof and broke my hand, so obtain retaliation for me from the wind. Then Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd عليه السلام summoned the wind and said to it: What caused you to do what you did to this woman? It said: You have spoken truly, O Prophet of Allah. The Lord of Might, Exalted is He, sent me to the ship of the people of so-and-so so that I might save it from sinking, and it had nearly sunk. So I went forth in my force and haste to carry out what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded me. I passed by this woman while she was upon her roof, and I struck against her without intending her, so she fell and her hand was broken.

He said: “So Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd عليه السلام said: My Lord, by what shall I judge concerning the wind? Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: O Sulaymān, judge that the compensation for the breaking of this woman’s hand is upon the owners of the ship which the wind saved from sinking, for indeed no one among the worlds is wronged in My presence.”

key_terms.دِيَتُهُ: his blood-money, the financial compensation for wrongful death
key_terms.عَاقِلَتِهِ: his ʿāqilah, the paternal kin group legally responsible for certain compensations
key_terms.مُسْتَعْدِيَةً: seeking legal redress or complaint against another

ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for blood-money or injury compensation when accidental harm occurs while rescuing others?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning liability when harm occurs unintentionally during an urgent effort to rescue others. It rules that the blood-money or compensation falls upon those who benefited from the rescue, and it reinforces the judgment through the account of Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd عليه السلام and the wind.
